issues.note: Real, common error; the note explains only the for/since fault, a small point.
Synonym plus compare with a difference note is defensible; the repetition is slightly redundant.
Means a length of time after since; the wording is loose but not truly misleading.
Correction must be the present perfect: have lived or have been living.
Correct: 'am living ... since' is wrong; present perfect needed.
The note is self-contradictory: 'has been' is not past simple; the trap is unclear.
The correction contradicts the note's own present perfect rule.
Same muddled tense test in the semantic adaptation note.
The since clause takes the past simple: since I last saw him.
Hedged with 'usually' and 'also'; the regional description is accurate.
Correctly names both contradictions: the example and the learner-error correction.
'have last seen' after since is unnatural; use the past simple.

findings.F1: The learner-error correction 'I am living here since I was ten' is still wrong; it needs the present perfect.
findings.F2: The example 'since I have last seen him' uses the present perfect in the since clause instead of the past simple.
findings.F3: The semantic adaptation note's tense test is muddled: it calls 'has been' past simple and states no clear trap.
